reason: The warm afternoon sets up the situation where the body may need to cool itself.
expectation: The body will respond to the warm surroundings, leading toward sweating.

effect: The warming skin sends temperature information toward the brain, so I can now follow the cooling response.
reaction: The picture makes it clearer that the body senses warming before responding.
reason: Sweat glands are the obvious next part of the goal to cool the body through evaporation.
expectation: The warming signal will activate the sweat glands and put sweat on the skin.

effect: Sweat glands were not the next pairing; skin vessels widened first, bringing more blood and heat near the surface.
reaction: I was surprised that circulation came before sweating.
reason: The goal still calls for sweat, and the glands are available after the circulation change.
expectation: The sweat glands will produce sweat on the skin.

effect: The glands have put sweat on the skin; evaporation is still needed to carry heat away.
reaction: The distinction between sweating and evaporation is clearer now.
reason: Air at the skin is pictured carrying water away, matching the remaining goal.
expectation: Sweat will evaporate and carry heat away from the body.

effect: Evaporation carried heat away, and the new goal shifts to conserving and making heat in the cold.
reaction: The fading sweat signal shows the cooling response easing as temperature returns toward its earlier range.
reason: The cold evening sets up the newly stated cold response, just as the warm afternoon set up cooling.
expectation: The body will sense the colder surroundings and begin a cold response.

effect: Cooling skin now sends information to the brain, and sweating has decreased.
reaction: The reduced sweating makes sense as the surroundings cool.
reason: Skin vessels changed during warming, so they may also help conserve heat in the cold.
expectation: The skin vessels will narrow, reducing blood flow near the surface and heat loss.

alternatives.reason: Muscle could help make heat, but I expect the vessel response first.

effect: Narrower skin vessels reduce heat loss but do not make heat, so the heat-making part remains.
reaction: The comparison makes clear that conserving heat and making it are different responses.
reason: Skeletal muscle is the remaining visible part that could help the body make heat.
expectation: The muscles will produce heat, possibly by shivering.

effect: Muscle contractions use energy and produce heat, completing the cold response alongside reduced heat loss from narrowed vessels.
reaction: It was satisfying to see how shivering and the skin vessels do different jobs.

mostWorthwhile.text: Comparing the cold vessel response with shivering was most worthwhile: one reduces heat loss while the other makes heat.

leastWorthwhile.text: Setting up the warm and cold conditions felt predictable, although it made the sequence easy to follow.

surprise.text: I expected sweating immediately, but the game had the skin vessels widen first.

arbitrary.text: Requiring the vessel change before sweating felt like an unexplained ordering rule; I understood both responses but not why the game required that order.

continue.text: I would probably continue: comparing the two temperature responses made the connections clear, though the sequence was fairly guided.
